title: Annotatio V §.III: invent double corporal eating; restrict Christ’s-body eating to mouth alone — call it Oral
pass_a_gloss: Of which the latter, that it may appear less Capernaite, (1) they restrict to the body’s mouth alone, ordering the gate of the teeth, the throat’s swallowing, and introduction into the stomach to be far away from here — and so greeting their Corporal Eating of Christ’s Body, from the denomination of the corporal mouth alone, as Oral.
pass_b_english: To look less Capernaite they restrict the second corporal eating to the mouth alone — teeth’s gate, throat-swallow, and stomach entry ordered far off.
From the mouth’s name alone they salute that corporal eating of Christ’s Body as Oral.
source_text: quarum posterior, ut minùs appareat Capernaitica (1) ad solum os corporis restringunt, Januam dentium, gutturis deglutitionem & in stomachum intromissionem hinc procul abesse jubentes, eóque Corporalem Corporis Christi Manducationem suam, à solius oris corporalis denominatione, Oralem salutantes.

lemmas.gloss: restrict to the body’s mouth alone

notes: Oral = mouth-only corporal of Christ’s body.
